realizes.rationale: The contract version field is the build's one source of the pinned host.
This file is the contract the pin checker reads, so the answer's shape is stated here.

1.note: The contract file consumed by the host pin.

2.note: Official v26.11.1 distribution checksums identify the selected linux-x64 archive digest. Re-fetched 2026-10-28T06:12Z: the file still publishes node-v26.11.1-linux-x64.tar.xz as 3883bfc73f9a680ca4eab04b196068aaaab1373ffa77d8fc1a4408222495b651, which is the digest this contract retains.

3.note: MIK-R107 v1 rule 1 asks the contract to name the newest 26.x.y that nodejs.org lists on the day of the build, with each archive's address and SHA-256 from the official SHASUMS256.txt. On 2026-10-08, the build day, the newest was v26.11.1, and v26.11.1 is what this contract names — the pin is what satisfying the rule left behind. Re-fetched 2026-10-28T06:12Z the newest is v26.12.1, so the rule was satisfied on its build day and the contract does not claim to satisfy it today.
